brief.subject: Covenant sees double-digit 2027 rate hikes; Arkansas blitz
brief.headline: Covenant CEO Expects Double-Digit 2027 Contract Hikes as Roadside Enforcement Tightens
brief.dek: Truckload contract rates may climb again in 2027, Arkansas runs a major enforcement blitz, and border trucking faces new pressures.
brief.lede: Covenant Logistics' CEO expects double-digit truckload contract rate increases in 2027, a sign shippers may face another year of rising costs.

sections.heading: Contract Rates Seen Climbing in 2027
bullets: Double-digit truckload contract hikes are expected in 2027, per Covenant Logistics CEO David Parker.
That would follow another year of substantial contract increases, giving small carriers leverage in upcoming rate talks.
Freight cycles since 2000 have behaved more like random shocks than clockwork, so plan for surprises.

sections.heading: Arkansas Blitz Hits Drivers Hard
bullets: 183 English-language proficiency violations were written during a two-day Arkansas enforcement operation.
44 criminal arrests and 74 immigration violations also resulted within 48 hours.
Expect English proficiency checks at roadside stops; make sure every driver can handle inspector questions.

sections.heading: Border Trucking Under Pressure
bullets: Cabotage enforcement is emerging as a threat to cross-border trucking operations.
50% toll cut on the Colombia Bridge from Nuevo León aims to draw more cross-border truck traffic.
Mexican truckers paused their nationwide strike but want measurable highway security gains from negotiations.

sections.heading: New Walmart DC Near San Antonio
bullets: $400M distribution center planned in Cibolo, Texas, spanning more than 744,000 square feet.
425 jobs expected, with groundbreaking slated for February, pointing to future regional freight demand.

sections.heading: Fed Holds; Autonomous Trucks Lag
bullets: The Fed kept its main rate steady despite accelerating inflation, so equipment financing costs stay elevated.
Two Fed policymakers dissented in favor of a 0.25 percentage point hike.
Aurora posted a $257 million operating loss on $3 million in revenue and cut its full-year forecast.
Aurora still says it will produce more than 1000 trucks in 2027.
